APL synapses project · step-by-step reports · Report 11 · 2026-11-04

A local, non-spiking APL in the KC model

QuestionIf APL is non-spiking, so that its inhibition stays near where it was excited, does it reshape the KC representation (the rank order of odor-pair similarity with inhibition on versus off) more like TNT vs TNT3c than one uniform APL or an APL weighted by per-KC synapse counts?

Reports 07 and 09 found that blocking APL in the data (TNT vs the TNT3c control) reorders odor pairs by similarity more than the model does: the rank correlation between blocked and intact similarity is 0.87 in the data (about 0.92 after correcting for recording noise) but 0.972 (ORN input) and 0.979 (GH146) in the model with one uniform APL. That model treats APL as one unit with one activity per odor. APL is thought to be non-spiking, and its activity can stay local within its arbor (Amin et al. 2020, eLife). This report builds a version of the model in which inhibition spreads passively along APL's actual skeleton and fades with distance, and asks whether that reorders the pairs more. Hemibrain and male CNS only (3 mushroom bodies), with the corrected calyx and the new claws.

What changed in this revision (2026-11-04)

The main results use the corrected calyx, the new claws and the new ORN table; the earlier version is compared at the end.

New: why θ = 1, what the C matrix is, and Equation 3 with every variable defined and worked through on a mock tree.

1What "non-spiking" means for the model

A spiking neuron turns local input into all-or-none action potentials that reach every part of the cell at full size, so "one activity per odor" is a fair description. A non-spiking neuron like APL instead carries graded voltage changes that spread passively and shrink with distance. In the simplest passive cable, a steady signal injected at one point falls off with distance ddd as e−d/λe^{-d/\lambda}e−d/λ. The length constant λ\lambdaλ of APL's fine calyx branches has not been measured, so the model scans it from 2 µm (very local) to 200 µm (almost global), and λ=∞\lambda = \inftyλ=∞ gives back the one-unit APL.

Distances are along the skeleton, not straight lines. Report 10 showed that APL's calyx arbor comes in several sub-arbors joined farther down, so two points a few µm apart in space can be over 100 µm apart along APL. For random pairs of a KC → APL site and an APL → KC site in the calyx the median distance is 198 µm (hemibrain R), 235 µm (male CNS L), 155 µm (male CNS R) (Figure 1a).

2The model, step by step

2.1Step 1: KC input and pinning (unchanged from Report 07)

Each KC's input is its claws' PN synapse shares times the glomeruli's ORN (or GH146) responses, with negative responses set to 0. Each odor's input is scaled by a gain gog_ogo​ so that, with APL blocked and θ=1\theta = 1θ=1, the fraction of KCs responding equals that odor's TNT fraction. Report 07 explains this pinning in full; it is the same here, so all versions start from identical blocked responses ykoblocked=[xko−1]+y^{\mathrm{blocked}}_{ko} = [x_{ko} - 1]_+ykoblocked​=[xko​−1]+​.

2.2Step 2: feedback through a coupling matrix

With APL intact, each KC is inhibited by an amount that depends on the activity of all KCs, through the coupling matrix MMM:

yko  =  [ xko−θ−a∑jMkj yjo]+(1)y_{ko} \;=\; \Big[\, x_{ko} - \theta - a \sum_{j} M_{kj}\, y_{jo} \Big]_+ \tag{1}yko​=[xko​−θ−aj∑​Mkj​yjo​]+​(1)
Solved for each odor separately; the responses appear on both sides, so the solution is the self-consistent steady state.

Why θ = 1. Because each odor's input is pinned (Step 1), the threshold can be any positive number: the gains gog_ogo​ scale the inputs to it. Setting θ = 1 only fixes the units, so xkox_{ko}xko​ is measured in "threshold units" (1 = exactly at threshold).

Every version has this form and differs only in MMM. The versions:

  • U, uniform: Mkj=1/NM_{kj} = 1/NMkj​=1/N. APL sums all KC activity and inhibits every KC equally. This is version U of Reports 05 and 07.
  • C, per-KC counts: Mkj=ukvj/NM_{kj} = u_k v_j / NMkj​=uk​vj​/N. KC jjj excites APL in proportion to its KC → APL synapses, and KC kkk is inhibited in proportion to its APL → KC synapses, but APL is still one unit with one activity. This "C matrix" is version C of Reports 05 and 07 written as a matrix: putting it into Equation 1 gives a∑jMkj yjo=a uk⋅1N∑jvj yjo=a uk Aoa\sum_j M_{kj}\,y_{jo} = a\,u_k \cdot \frac{1}{N}\sum_j v_j\,y_{jo} = a\,u_k\,A_oa∑j​Mkj​yjo​=auk​⋅N1​∑j​vj​yjo​=auk​Ao​, one APL activity AoA_oAo​ (the vvv-weighted mean KC response) applied to KC kkk in proportion to uku_kuk​. It is written as a matrix only to compare it with the local matrices, which have the same form but let the coupling depend on where on APL the synapses are.
  • local, length constant λ\lambdaλ: Equation 2.
Mkj  =  c∑s ∈ out(k)  ∑t ∈ in(j)e−d(s,t)/λ(2)M_{kj} \;=\; c \sum_{s \,\in\, \mathrm{out}(k)} \; \sum_{t \,\in\, \mathrm{in}(j)} e^{-d(s,t)/\lambda} \tag{2}Mkj​=cs∈out(k)∑​t∈in(j)∑​e−d(s,t)/λ(2)
KC jjj's activity enters APL at each of its KC → APL synapses ttt, spreads along APL with decay e−d/λe^{-d/\lambda}e−d/λ, and inhibits KC kkk at each APL → KC synapse sss on kkk.

As λ→∞\lambda \to \inftyλ→∞ every exponential becomes 1, and Mkj=c ∣out(k)∣ ∣in(j)∣M_{kj} = c\,|\mathrm{out}(k)|\,|\mathrm{in}(j)|Mkj​=c∣out(k)∣∣in(j)∣, which is C (checked: correlation 1.000 in all three mushroom bodies). So C is the local model with an infinitely long length constant, and the local versions differ from C only in where on APL each KC's synapses are. The constant ccc sets the mean of MMM to that of C, so that the gain aaa has comparable values across versions; the calibration in Step 4 would absorb any constant anyway.

What counts as a site

Only calyx synapses are used, as for C (per-KC counts are calyx only, Yang 2026-10-21). APL's side of each synapse is placed at the nearest node of the APL skeleton: the T-bar for APL → KC, the PSD for KC → APL (median snap distance 0.4 µm in hemibrain R, 0.8 µm in male CNS L, 0.8 µm in male CNS R).

Two sites at the same node have d=0d = 0d=0. Snap distances are not added to ddd, so at λ = 2 µm the result depends on the skeleton's resolution.

2.3Step 3: computing M on the tree

A direct sum over all pairs of sites (tens of thousands of each per mushroom body) would need every pairwise distance. Because a skeleton is a tree, the same sums can be computed exactly in two passes. First the tree is reduced to the part that joins the synapse nodes, with chains of unbranched nodes merged into single edges of summed length ℓv\ell_vℓv​ (16,742 nodes remain in hemibrain R, 6,579 nodes remain in male CNS L, 5,755 nodes remain in male CNS R). Let nvjn_{vj}nvj​ be the number of KC → APL sites of KC jjj at node vvv, and κv=e−ℓv/λ\kappa_v = e^{-\ell_v/\lambda}κv​=e−ℓv​/λ. Then:

upvj=nvj+∑w ∈ children(v)κw upwj,Φvj=upvj (1−κv2)+κv Φparent(v), j,Φroot,j=uproot,j(3)\text{up}_{vj} = n_{vj} + \sum_{w \,\in\, \mathrm{children}(v)} \kappa_w\, \text{up}_{wj}, \qquad \Phi_{vj} = \text{up}_{vj}\,(1 - \kappa_v^2) + \kappa_v\, \Phi_{\mathrm{parent}(v),\,j}, \quad \Phi_{\mathrm{root},j} = \text{up}_{\mathrm{root},j} \tag{3}upvj​=nvj​+w∈children(v)∑​κw​upwj​,Φvj​=upvj​(1−κv2​)+κv​Φparent(v),j​,Φroot,j​=uproot,j​(3)
Pass 1 runs from the leaves up; pass 2 from the root down. Φvj=∑t∈in(j)e−d(v,t)/λ\Phi_{vj} = \sum_{t \in \mathrm{in}(j)} e^{-d(v,t)/\lambda}Φvj​=∑t∈in(j)​e−d(v,t)/λ, the signal from KC jjj at node vvv.

Why it works: the path from vvv to a site ttt below vvv stays below vvv, and its weight is the product of the κ\kappaκ of its edges, which pass 1 collects. A site not below vvv is reached through vvv's parent; pass 2 takes the parent's total, multiplies by κv\kappa_vκv​ for the edge, and removes the part that came from below vvv itself (that part crossed the edge twice, hence κv2\kappa_v^2κv2​). Finally Mkj=c∑s∈out(k)ΦsjM_{kj} = c\sum_{s \in \mathrm{out}(k)} \Phi_{s j}Mkj​=c∑s∈out(k)​Φsj​. Check: at λ = 10 µm, Φ\PhiΦ for 40 random KCs at 60 random nodes was also computed by brute force (shortest paths on the tree); the largest difference relative to the largest value was 4e-16, 1e-16, 3e-16 (rounding error).

2.4Equation 3, every variable, with a mock tree

What it computes. For the local model we need Φvj\Phi_{vj}Φvj​: the total signal that KC jjj's inputs to APL produce at a point vvv of APL, each input decayed by its distance along APL, Φvj=∑t∈in(j)e−d(v,t)/λ\Phi_{vj} = \sum_{t \in \text{in}(j)} e^{-d(v,t)/\lambda}Φvj​=∑t∈in(j)​e−d(v,t)/λ. Summing it over KC kkk's output sites gives MkjM_{kj}Mkj​. Equation 3 computes Φ\PhiΦ for every node without ever listing distances, using one fact: the decay along a path is the product of the decays of its edges, e−(ℓ1+ℓ2)/λ=e−ℓ1/λ e−ℓ2/λe^{-(\ell_1 + \ell_2)/\lambda} = e^{-\ell_1/\lambda}\,e^{-\ell_2/\lambda}e−(ℓ1​+ℓ2​)/λ=e−ℓ1​/λe−ℓ2​/λ.

2.5Step 4: one APL gain per version, and the solver

For each mushroom body, input table and version, the gain aaa is found by bisection (32 halvings after doubling until it is large enough) so that the mean fraction of KCs responding over odors equals TNT3c's, 6.83% for the 16 odors. Equation 1 is solved per odor with an exact active-set method: guess which KCs respond, solve the linear equations (I+aMSS) yS=xS−θ(I + aM_{SS})\,y_S = x_S - \theta(I+aMSS​)yS​=xS​−θ for that set SSS, add KCs whose net input is still above threshold and drop KCs whose solution is negative, and repeat until the set stops changing. If the set cycles or the result fails a residual check, a damped fixed-point iteration is used instead. Both solvers were run on the same cases and agree (gains equal to 4 decimals, responses within about 10⁻⁶). With feedback this strong a threshold-linear network could in principle have more than one steady state; the solver starts from the blocked responses and finds one.

2.6Step 5: readouts

  • Rank order ρrank\rho_{\mathrm{rank}}ρrank​: for each mushroom body, the Spearman correlation over odor pairs between blocked and intact cosine similarity, then the mean over the three mushroom bodies. Data: TNT vs TNT3c, 0.869 over the 16 odors, 0.873 over the 13 GH146 odors; corrected for recording noise about 0.92 (Report 09).
  • Pattern rrr: the model's change in similarity per pair (blocked − intact, similarity averaged over the three mushroom bodies) correlated with the data's change (TNT − TNT3c). The data's own reliability limits this to about 0.84 (Report 07).
  • Size: the mean change in similarity over pairs (data: 0.178 for the 16 odors).

2.7Step 6: a null for the real placement of each KC on APL

Is it the real position of each KC's synapses on APL that matters, or only how local the inhibition is? For the local version with the best pattern rrr, KCs are shuffled within their class (αβ, α′β′, γ): KC kkk gets the APL sites of KC π(k)\pi(k)π(k), which turns MMM into Mπ(k)π(j)M_{\pi(k)\pi(j)}Mπ(k)π(j)​. This keeps the arbor, the class composition and the locality, and only breaks which KC sits where. 100 shuffles per mushroom body, each recalibrated. One-sided ppp = (1 + shuffles at least as extreme) / 101.

Caveat on the null

The λ tested is the one with the best rrr among the local versions, picked before the shuffles, so the ppp value does not correct for having tried seven λ values.

2.8Step 7: local inhibition of PN boutons too

APL also inhibits the PN boutons (about 10% of its calyx output synapses, Report 04). The second script adds this route. Bouton bbb receives the local APL signal at its APL → PN synapses, per PN → KC synapse it makes onto claws, and divides its output:

3What shorter length constants do to the coupling

At λ = 100 µm each hemibrain KC is still inhibited by about 68% of all KCs, at 10 µm by about 27% and at 2 µm by about 5.6% (about 99 KCs). Self-inhibition stays small even at 2 µm (3.1%), because a KC's own APL synapses are only a few of the many near any site. Short λ also shifts the coupling toward KCs of the same class (42% of MMM at λ = ∞, 62% at 2 µm in hemibrain), since KCs of one class share parts of the calyx.

Answer

Rank order: no. A local APL on the KCs leaves ρrank\rho_{\mathrm{rank}}ρrank​ at 0.958–0.972 (ORN) and 0.953–0.977 (GH146), like U (0.972, 0.979) and far from the data's ≈ 0.92. Only inhibition placed entirely on the PN boutons gets close: 0.931 (ORN), 0.923 (GH146). At the boutons' real share of APL's output (KC + boutons) it is back to 0.956–0.970, 0.961–0.977.

Pattern: somewhat. Short length constants raise rrr with the data's pattern of changes: best local on KCs 0.557 at 2 µm (ORN), 0.573 at 2 µm (GH146), vs U 0.494 / 0.405 and C 0.494 / 0.447. Whether the real placement of each KC on APL matters beyond locality depends on the input table (it beats within-class shuffles only where ppp ≤ 0.05): ORN: rrr 0.557 vs shuffles 0.490 (5–95% 0.26–0.64), ppp = 0.32; GH146: rrr 0.573 vs shuffles 0.299 (5–95% 0.02–0.49), ppp = 0.02.

Size: no. The mean change in similarity of U and the local versions on KCs is 31%–44% of the data's (ORN), 15%–27% of the data's (GH146).

For the pattern, the real wiring beats the shuffles for GH146 and not for ORN, so part of the gain is locality itself. Rank order with real wiring vs shuffles: ORN 0.958 vs 0.979, ppp = 0.01; GH146 0.953 vs 0.979, ppp = 0.01. The real wiring reorders a little more than the shuffles (by up to 0.026), but it still stays above the data's noise-corrected ≈ 0.92 (gap 0.033 or more).

6What this means, and caveats

  • A non-spiking APL whose inhibition stays local predicts which odor pairs change most when APL is blocked better than a uniform or count-weighted APL does. Whether the real positions of each KC's synapses add to this beyond locality is mixed: the real wiring beats within-class shuffles for GH146, now (ppp = 0.02); ORN, earlier version (ppp = 0.02); GH146, earlier version (ppp = 0.01), but not for ORN, now (ppp = 0.32). This supports the idea that APL's local structure shapes the effect of inhibition on which pairs change.
  • It does not make inhibition reorder the pairs as much as in the data. In this model, inhibition applied at the KCs, whatever its spatial range, keeps the order of similarities nearly intact (Report 09 shows when that is expected). Inhibition applied before the KCs, on the PN boutons, changes the input itself and reorders more; at the boutons' real synapse share it is too weak to matter here.
  • The model's mean changes are 31%–44% (ORN, now), 15%–27% (GH146, now), 24%–44% (ORN, earlier version), 14%–30% (GH146, earlier version) of the data's, so something not in the model (e.g. stronger or nonlinear inhibition, KC-to-KC or other interactions, recording noise that differs between genotypes) also contributes.
Caveats

λ = 2 µm is close to the skeleton's resolution (synapses snap 0.4–0.8 µm to nodes, median), so the shortest λ values are approximate.

The best λ was picked before the shuffle test; the ppp values do not correct for that choice.

Synapse counts stand in for synaptic strength, and the passive decay e−d/λe^{-d/\lambda}e−d/λ ignores branch thickness and the signal's time course (a steady state is assumed).

A threshold-linear network with strong feedback can have more than one steady state; the solver finds the one reached from the blocked responses.
